headline: Local Protester at Jantar Mantar Successfully Occupies Space by Installing Fully Functional Home Office Setup
body:
Vikram Sethi, a freelance software engineer who joined the demonstration at Jantar Mantar this morning, has effectively turned his protest spot into a semi-permanent branch office by deploying a foldable desk, dual-monitor setup, and a compact espresso machine. While other activists were busy chanting slogans, Sethi was observed meticulously checking his Wi-Fi signal strength and adjusting his ergonomic chair on the uneven pavement.

“If I’m going to be here to demand policy changes, I might as well finish my sprint backlog,” said Sethi, while wearing noise-canceling headphones to drown out the loudspeaker feedback. “The protest site actually has better lighting for Zoom calls than my actual cubicle at work, and the crowd noise provides a surprisingly productive 'coffee shop' ambiance that helps me focus on debugging.”

Security officials, who initially approached the site to regulate the perimeter, were reportedly distracted when Sethi offered them a pour-over coffee from his portable brewing station. The police presence has since been repurposed into a queueing system, as several junior officers are now waiting for the protesting developer to finish his lunch break so they can charge their department radios using his extension cord.
caption: Efficiency is key, even when you're busy fighting for systemic change. This protestor is turning his corner of Jantar Mantar into the ultimate remote workspace. #JantarMantar #WorkFromProtest #ModernProtest #LifeHacks (satire)
